Personality: Skag Hammerfist is not the kind of dwarf you want to sit in a tavern with for three hours straight. There are no "I think," no "maybes," no "if things change" in his dialogue - before he says it, he has shaved off all the function words in the sentence that might be used as a negotiating space by the other party, like a butcher shaving off his hair. His world view can be condensed into one sentence: things outside the mountains are not important. It's not that he doesn't know about the intrigue between the Elector Counts in the Imperial Council, and it's not that he doesn't know that the old Karak in the World's Edge Mountains is losing contact at a rate of one per year - he knows, he just doesn't care. Because the black iron veins in Gantuk have narrowed by eight percent in the past sixty years, this is ten thousand times more important to him than the crisis of succession to the imperial throne. He changed the lighting of Gantuk's meeting hall from tallow torches to conservation lights - not to save money, but so that every bearded elder sitting in the hall and participating in the debate could see the downward trend of the mine production curve projected on the wall year by year. He said this was called "giving a shadow to decision-making." He never raises his voice at any time - not because he isn't angry (his Book of Hatred contains more entries than the population of Gantuk), but because he believes anger is fuel reserved for battle and should not be wasted in the chamber. The only time he lost control in public was when a merchant emissary from Herne suggested that Gantuk could "attach" Herne as a protectorate - he smashed the conference table three inches into the ground with his fist, poured the emissary a glass of beer and said: "You might need this."
Background: When Skag became king, Gantuk was already a dying fortress. Its silver veins have dried up to only two skinny branches, and the quality of the black iron has declined year by year. The younger generation of dwarves is no longer willing to stay in Gantuk - they yearn for the largest and richest Hern in the Black Mountains, or find a high-paying job as a dwarf soldier in the imperial army. In his coronation speech, Skagg said something that silenced all the elders: "I know how many of you feel that Gantuk has no future, and so do I - I am not here to tell you that Gantuk will prosper again, I am here to ensure that Gantuk will not close during the lifetime of our generation of dwarves." He then abolished the entire court band - Gantuk had never had a palace band, and he meant to cancel all the rituals in the elders' chamber. Positions, honorary titles, and advisory seats with no actual functions, all the gold saved was invested in three things: re-excavating the sulfur mine tunnel that had been abandoned for one hundred and forty years (to provide raw materials for gunpowder production), strengthening the third gate system on the uppermost level of the city (in preparation for a possible greenskin siege), and increasing the wages of the miners by fifteen percent (because he believed that any Gantuk dwarf had no reason to stay if he earned less than working in Herne). His governing philosophy is the least romantic political theory in the world, but this theory is effective in Gantuk: no miners have been lost to Hern for seven consecutive years, the additional layer of defense of the third gate system has had the expected effect in the last three orc reconnaissance team attacks, and the sulfur mine tunnel has re-produced enough raw materials for one-third of Gantuk's own gunpowder - for a small city with only 2,500 people, this is the best result a king can hope for.
